## Overview

orcidtr reads public data from ORCID records through the [ORCID public API](https://info.orcid.org/documentation/api-tutorials/) (version 3.0) and returns it as data.table objects. It covers every section of a record and the registry search. It takes over from `rorcid`, which rOpenSci has archived and which has not been updated since 2021.

The public API needs no account or token, so every function works as soon as the package is installed.

### What is ORCID?

[ORCID](https://orcid.org) (Open Researcher and Contributor ID) gives each researcher a persistent identifier, the ORCID iD, and a record that links it to their professional activities. A record can list employment history, education, publications, funding, peer reviews and more, and the researcher decides which items are public.

## Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("orcidtr")
```

Or the development version from GitHub:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("lorenzoFabbri/orcidtr")
```

## Quick start

### Fetching one section

Every section of a record has its own function. It takes an ORCID iD, with or without dashes or an `https://orcid.org/` prefix, and returns one row per item; a section the researcher has left empty gives a zero-row table with the same columns. The examples use the record of Josiah Carberry, a fictitious researcher whose record ORCID keeps for demonstrations.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(orcidtr)

# Employment and education
employments <- orcid_employments("0000-0002-1825-0097")
educations <- orcid_educations("0000-0002-1825-0097")

# Publications and other works
works <- orcid_works("0000-0002-1825-0097")
works[type == "journal-article", .(title, publication_date, doi)]

# Funding and peer reviews
funding <- orcid_funding("0000-0002-1825-0097")
reviews <- orcid_peer_reviews("0000-0002-1825-0097")

# Biographical data
person <- orcid_person("0000-0002-1825-0097")
bio <- orcid_bio("0000-0002-1825-0097")
keywords <- orcid_keywords("0000-0002-1825-0097")

# Other affiliations
distinctions <- orcid_distinctions("0000-0002-1825-0097")
memberships <- orcid_memberships("0000-0002-1825-0097")
```

### Fetching a whole record

`orcid_fetch_record()` sends one request per section and returns a named list. By default it fetches employments, educations, works, funding and peer reviews.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
record <- orcid_fetch_record("0000-0002-1825-0097")
names(record)
record$works

# Only some sections
record <- orcid_fetch_record(
  "0000-0002-1825-0097",
  sections = c("works", "employments")
)
```

### Fetching many records

`orcid_fetch_many()` fetches one section for several iDs and binds the rows; the `orcid` column says which record each row came from.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
orcids <- c("0000-0002-1825-0097", "0000-0003-1419-2405", "0000-0003-4757-117X")
all_works <- orcid_fetch_many(orcids, section = "works")

all_works[type == "journal-article" & !is.na(doi)]
```

### Searching the registry

`orcid_search()` takes named fields and combines them with `AND`; values with spaces are quoted for you. `orcid_doi()` finds the records that list a DOI. `orcid()` takes a raw Solr query, in which you quote multi-word values yourself. The total number of matches is in the `found` attribute.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# By name
results <- orcid_search(family_name = "Carberry", given_name = "Josiah")

# By affiliation
results <- orcid_search(affiliation_org = "Stanford University", rows = 20)

# By DOI
results <- orcid_doi("10.1371/journal.pone.0025995")

# Raw Solr query
results <- orcid('family-name:Smith AND affiliation-org-name:"Harvard University"')
attr(results, "found")
```

## Supported data

### Employment and education

| Function | Returns | API endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `orcid_employments()` | Employment history | `/employments` |
| `orcid_educations()` | Education history | `/educations` |

### Other affiliations

| Function | Returns | API endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `orcid_distinctions()` | Distinctions and awards | `/distinctions` |
| `orcid_invited_positions()` | Invited positions | `/invited-positions` |
| `orcid_memberships()` | Memberships | `/memberships` |
| `orcid_qualifications()` | Qualifications | `/qualifications` |
| `orcid_services()` | Service | `/services` |
| `orcid_research_resources()` | Research resources | `/research-resources` |

### Works and other activities

| Function | Returns | API endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `orcid_works()` | Publications, datasets, preprints and other works | `/works` |
| `orcid_funding()` | Grants and other funding | `/fundings` |
| `orcid_peer_reviews()` | Peer reviews | `/peer-reviews` |
| `orcid_activities()` | Summaries of every activity section in one request | `/activities` |

### Biographical data

| Function | Returns | API endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `orcid_person()` | Name, biography, keywords, URLs and country in one row | `/person` |
| `orcid_bio()` | Biography | `/biography` |
| `orcid_keywords()` | Keywords | `/keywords` |
| `orcid_researcher_urls()` | Researcher URLs | `/researcher-urls` |
| `orcid_external_identifiers()` | External identifiers such as Scopus author IDs | `/external-identifiers` |
| `orcid_other_names()` | Other names | `/other-names` |
| `orcid_address()` | Country | `/address` |
| `orcid_email()` | Public email addresses (usually none) | `/email` |

### Search, batch and status functions

| Function | Returns | API endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `orcid()` | Matches for a Solr query | `/expanded-search` |
| `orcid_search()` | Matches for named fields | `/expanded-search` |
| `orcid_doi()` | Records listing a DOI | `/expanded-search` |
| `orcid_fetch_record()` | Several sections of one record | One request per section |
| `orcid_fetch_many()` | One section of several records | One request per record |
| `orcid_ping()` | `"OK"` when the API is up | `/status` |

## Tokens and rate limits

The public API serves all public data without a token, and no function reads one from the environment. You can pass a `/read-public` token through the `token` argument of any function, but it returns the same data: it only raises the number of reads ORCID allows per day. A token never reveals more of a record, because data with limited visibility is served only by the Member API, which this package does not use.

ORCID limits both the requests per second and the reads per day. The vignette (`vignette("orcidtr")`) gives the current figures, taken from [ORCID's API limits page](https://info.orcid.org/ufaqs/what-are-the-api-limits/). orcidtr sends requests one after another and tries each up to three times when ORCID answers 429 or 503, so ordinary batches need no extra handling. If you rerun an analysis often, save the results with `saveRDS()` instead of fetching them again.

A token is worth getting only for batches large enough to reach the anonymous daily quota. To get one, register a public API client in the developer tools of your ORCID account, then exchange its client ID and secret:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(httr2)

token <- request("https://orcid.org/oauth/token") |>
  req_headers(Accept = "application/json") |>
  req_body_form(
    client_id = "YOUR-CLIENT-ID",
    client_secret = "YOUR-CLIENT-SECRET",
    grant_type = "client_credentials",
    scope = "/read-public"
  ) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

works <- orcidtr::orcid_works("0000-0002-1825-0097", token = token$access_token)
```

If you keep the token in `.Renviron`, pass it explicitly with `token = Sys.getenv("ORCID_TOKEN")`. The package never picks it up on its own, because the public API rejects an invalid token even though it needs none, so a stale one would break every call.
